sentences.text:
Shri
M.M. Jaiswal - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Yash Soni - Deputy Advocate General for the State.

Appellant has filed fifth application i.e. I.A. No.26194/2025 an application under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973/Section 430 for the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail.

2. Appellant has been convicted under Sections 376-D, 450, 323 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life, R.I. for seven years, R.I. for seven years with fine of Rs.1,00,000/-, Rs.10,000/-, Rs.500/- respectively, with default stipulations.
3. Prosecution story in brief is that appellant along with other co- accused person namely Ramkumar @ Michku is said to have committed gang rape with prosecutrix when she was alone in the house.
Prosecutrix is mentally challenged.
When mother of prosecutrix returned she discovered about incident and found a black purse under the cot.
She went to police station and lodged FIR.
Black purse found on spot was seized by police at police station.
In said purse photograph of appellant namely Rajesh @ Raju Agrawal was found.
Rajesh and Ramkumar @ Michku were arrested for committing offences under aforementioned 2 CRA-8124-2018 Sections.
4. Learned counsel appearing for appellant submitted that appellant was falsely implicated in the case.
Ramkumar @ Michku was Worker of Rajesh Agrawal.
He has kept visiting card and photograph in purse.
Purse belongs to Michku and not of Rajesh(present appellant).
Plea of alibi was taken by appellant but same has not been properly appreciated by trial Court.
No other evidence except a wallet which is said to have belonged to appellant was found on spot.
This is case of no evidence and jail sentence of appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
5. Learned Government Advocate appearing for State opposed the application and submitted that mother of prosecutrix has lodged report on same day.
Appellant has been named in the FIR.
Prosecutrix has received external injury on her body.
She was examined by doctor on the same day.
Purse of appellant was found on spot which was having his photograph in it.

Prosecutrix has Rajesh @ Raju Agrawal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44139482/
1 identified the appellant in Court and by signs showed that she was raped by him.

sentences.text: In these circumstances, application for suspension of sentence may be dismissed.
6. Heard the counsel for the parties.
7. First application i.e. IA No.6013/2021 was dismissed as infructuous on 06.07.2021.

Earlier three applications for suspension of sentence i.e. IA No.17724/2021, IA No.29093/2023 and IA No.18853/2025 were dismissed as withdrawn on 12.04.2023, 3 CRA-8124-2018 01.02.2024 and 29.08.2025 with liberty to file repeat application.
This is fifth application for suspension of sentence.
Earlier applications were not considered on merits and were dismissed in limine.
8. On going through the records of the case, it is found that only evidence which is available against appellant was wallet which was found on spot of incident by one Shanti Bai Bandevar (PW-2).
No other evidence is available against the appellant.
In FSL report dated 30.09.2015, sperms were not found on slide of prosecutrix(Article-A), her Salwar (Article-B) and on her underwear (Article-C).
Since, no sperms were found on said Articles, therefore, there is no question of conducting DNA examination.
Report of FSL is negative in respect of appellant.
Prosecutrix is mentally challenged.
She has identified appellant as Ashish.
In deposition, she has stated that rape was committed upon her by two persons.
One of the name i.e. Ramkumar @ Michku was rightly taken by the prosecutrix.
She says that other accused was one Ashish.
Though, she says that person in Court has committed rape upon her.
She also admits in Court that mother had tutored her to tell said fact in Court.
She had answered most of the suggestive questions in positive.
Doctor has given report (Ex.P/15) that she is 50% mentally challenged.
Court has made observation that she is not giving clear answer to questions put to her.
She is mentally weak and suffers from difficulty in speaking.
Her statement was recorded with help of expert.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case there has to 4 CRA-8124-2018 be some more evidence corroborating the evidence given by prosecutrix.
9. Now it is to been seen whether there is some corroboration of prosecutrix version from other evidence available on record.
FIR is said to have been lodged after the incident and appellant has been named in it.
Mother of prosecutrix (PW-5) stated that report and statement given to police was not made by her but by one Radheshyam Bandevar, who is a Journalist.
He is the person who has identified the photograph to be of Rajesh @ Raju Agrawal-appellant.
Person who saw the purse under the cot was Shanti Bai Bandevar (PW-2) and she has stated that door of house was open, she has found the purse near cot.
She has not seen what was inside the purse but in paragraph-4 of her deposition says that photograph was not of same person who was present in Court namely Rajesh Agrawal.
She was declared hostile by Court.
Purse was not produced before the Court for identification.
Mother of prosecutrix (PW- 5) says that nothing was discovered from inside the room.
She says that photograph of Rajesh was found under the Cot.
She does not states that purse was found in which photograph was kept.
She specifically states that report was lodged by Journalist- Radheshyam Bandevar and her statement was also recorded by him.
Shanti Bai Bandevar (PW-2) has also stated that she found the purse under the cot.

Ashok Bandevar (PW- Rajesh @ Raju Agrawal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44139482/
2 6) had admitted that he went along with Shanti Bai (PW-5) for lodging police report.

sentences.text: He has also identified that photograph was of Rajesh 5 CRA-8124-2018 Agrawal.
He was unable to tell color of said purse and whether purse was of leather or rexine.
He could not tell about other articles present in purse.
He only said that there was visiting cards in said purse.
He was unable to state about details of the photograph i.e. whether person in photograph was in shirt or t-shirt and whether person in photo was wearing spectacles or not.
He had admitted that similar purse can be found with other person also.
10. Considering the aforesaid evidence and material facts available on record, it is found that photograph is secondary evidence and not admissible until proved by the negative of the photographs.
Purse was not discovered on disclosure statement made by accused.
It is said to have been found on spot and was not collected from there by police.
It was taken to police station by the complainant and thereafter, is being used as evidence.
Evidentiary value of said purse is weak.
Person who has identified appellant-Rajesh @ Raju Agrawal in photograph was not able to give particulars about the photographs.
Purse was not produced before the Court and same has not been identified to have belonged to appellant-Rajesh Agrawal.
FIR is said to have been lodged by one Journalist-Ashok Bandevar and not by mother of prosecutrix.
FSL is negative, though prosecutrix was medically examined on the same day.
Sperms were not found on the clothes (Salwar and underwear) of prosecutrix nor on the slide which was prepared by the doctor form prosecutrix.
No other evidence is available 6 CRA-8124-2018 against the appellant.

11. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case and also the fact that appellant is in jail for about 10 years and hearing of appeal will take long time, I.A. No.26194/2025 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail, is allowed.

12. It is hereby directed that the custodial sentence awarded to the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and he shall be released on bail subject on depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited and on his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.
Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 17.06.2026 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.
13. Certified copy as per rules.
